-- args --
m
--target-version
-- want --
exit 2
-- stderr --
usage: report-module.sh <module-root> [--target-version x.y] [--console-dir <dir>] [--profile hmi|lan|both|unknown] [--legacy] [--wiring-map <file>] [--niagara-home <dir>] [--first-deploy] [--lint-only] [--write-baseline] [--no-baseline] [--feature-doc <file>]
  baseline: <module-root>/.report-baseline lists the FAIL rows the module already had, one key per line:
      <artifact>  <check>  <detail>
    the row without its status; in <detail> a path is cut to its file name and a number standing alone (a line
    number, a count) reads N, so a key survives unrelated edits. "#" lines and blank lines are ignored.
    With the file, FAIL rows are printed in two groups, NEW and BASE, after the other rows, and the verdict and
    the exit code read the NEW rows only; a line no FAIL row matches is a WARN "stale baseline line" row.
    Never baselined (always NEW): verify-module gate rows, schema-risk rows, a member that "exited N with no
    FAIL row" (a crash), triage-console lines.
  --write-baseline  write the file from this run's FAIL rows (sorted, de-duplicated); the exit code is the run's
  --no-baseline     ignore the file for this run
  --ready [--niagara-home <dir>] [--expect-niagara <ver>] [--expect-signer <alias>] [--json]
    the ready-to-load report of each built jar (<artifact>/build/libs): module, niagara-target, niagara-home,
    signer, verify-module, schema-risk, sha256 and mirror rows (an artifact with no built jar is one FAIL jar
    row), then "READY TO LOAD: <MOD> <version> for Niagara <x> (sha256 <12>)" and the post-load read-back,
    or "NOT READY" with the failing rows; exit 0 ready, 1 not ready, 3 env (an ERROR row, a module root that
    cannot be listed, or no built jar). --target-version and --first-deploy apply; it refuses every lint-run
    option (--lint-only, --write-baseline, --no-baseline, --console-dir, --profile, --legacy, --wiring-map,
    --feature-doc), and --json/--expect-* need --ready.
